text: Genesis 6 gives both terms without dilution: “Noah walked with God” in a world whose corruption is named without softness (Genesis 6:9). “Every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually” (Genesis 6:5); “the earth was filled with violence” (Genesis 6:11); Yahweh was sorry that he had made man (Genesis 6:6). Noah is not commissioned to reform that world. He is told to build. The proportions of the chapter matter here, since the ark receives the fuller description in its specifications and measurements (Genesis 6:14–16). Noah builds to a measure he did not set. The ark is first a set of dimensions before it is timber, and Noah’s part is summarized only this way: “according to all that God commanded him, so did he” (Genesis 6:22). Genesis 6 has already called him righteous (Genesis 6:9). In this chapter that righteousness appears as obedience, the willingness to build what God, having seen the whole world, says will be needed.
